intent: Test whether a larger drive wheel (radius 0.045 m, up from 0.040 m) lifts average speed enough to raise the finish rate and lower completion time, while keeping the best-supported sensor layout (5 sensors at y=0.07 m, ±0.036 m spread, 16 mm footprint), track 0.10 m and mass 0.5 kg from iteration 5. Single-variable change against iteration 5. Expected: oval finish rate at or above 95%, oval completion time below 1.7 s, and no rise in s-bend off-track exits.
learning: Hypotheses: (1) Radius 0.045 m keeps the oval finish rate at or above 95% and cuts oval completion time below 1.7 s. (2) If s-bend off-track exits rise while max_error stays at 0.06 m, speed is outrunning steering, so the next step is to return to radius 0.040 m and look at the forward offset. (3) If slalom line losses stay near 1.85, the slalom limit is sensor coverage or controller gain, not speed. Outer spread of ±0.045 m (iteration 8) and track 0.09 m (iteration 7) are ruled out.
rationale: Scores so far: iteration 5 (422.9) and iteration 6 (422.1) are the best designs. Both use 5 sensors at y=0.07 m, 16 mm footprint, track 0.10 m, radius 0.040 m. Iteration 6 cut mass to 0.4 kg and gave the same score, with worse s-bend progress (0.59 vs 0.72), so 0.5 kg stays. Iteration 7 (track 0.09 m) cut the oval finish rate to 60% and is ruled out. Iteration 8 (outer sensors at ±0.045 m) fell to 309: oval finish dropped to 65%, and slalom line losses (1.0) and progress did not improve on iteration 5. So I revert the spread to ±0.036 m. Wheel radius is the one drivetrain lever that has paid off consistently: 0.035 to 0.040 m raised oval finish from 65% to 80%, and mean oval time fell to about 1.7 s. Radius is also untested beyond 0.040 m. This iteration keeps the iteration 5 layout and sets radius to 0.045 m, the only change. Expected result: oval finish holds at or above 95%, completion time falls further, and the s-bend and slalom stay limited by off-track exits. The risk is that higher ground speed outruns the steering on tight bends, which would show as more s-bend off-track exits and a higher max_error.
